nodes.name: DevOps Foundations and Operating Mindset
core_concepts: What DevOps and SRE mean in practice
Availability, resilience, and software delivery flow
SLOs, toil reduction, and human-centered operations

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how a DevOps or SRE mindset changes the way a team handles deployments, incidents, and repeated operational work compared with a pure application-development mindset.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why does reducing toil not just improve productivity, but also reduce operational risk and increase service reliability?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands system operations as part of software delivery
Recognizes automation and reliability as engineering work
Can connect operational habits to service quality
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Start by identifying the recurring operational tasks that are painful or error-prone; those are the highest-value automation opportunities.

nodes.name: Linux, Shell, and System Administration Basics
core_concepts: Processes, daemons, permissions, and file systems

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: A service is failing intermittently and the logs show no obvious application error. Explain how you would inspect the system using basic Linux and shell tools to diagnose the issue.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do many production incidents begin as unexpected interactions between the application, the OS, and the network, even when the code itself appears correct?
key_evaluation_criteria: Uses shell and system tools confidently
Knows how to identify process and resource issues
Links OS-level observations to root cause analysis
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Learn how to inspect processes, CPU, memory, sockets, and logs before changing code or redeploying systems.

nodes.name: Version Control, Git, and CI/CD Pipelines
core_concepts: Pull requests, code review, and merge discipline

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Design a safe CI/CD workflow for a microservice that must run tests, static checks, and deployment validation before it reaches production.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why is speed in deployment only valuable when the pipeline creates predictable, reviewable, and recoverable changes?
key_evaluation_criteria: Uses version control and CI/CD correctly
Can explain pipeline stages and quality checks
Prevents unsafe or unreviewed code from reaching production
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Focus on fast feedback and auditable changes: build checks, pass/fail gates, and rollback plans are more valuable than ever-larger releases.

nodes.name: Networking, Security, and Proxying Basics
core_concepts: DNS, HTTP, HTTPS, TLS, SSH, SMTP, and email protocols
Firewall rules, white/grey listing, and access control
Proxying, reverse proxy, load balancing, caching

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: A service is reachable internally but not externally. Explain how you would isolate whether the problem is DNS, TLS, firewall, proxy, or application-level configuration.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do infrastructure and networking issues often look like application bugs until you trace the request path through the edge and proxy layers?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands request flow and edge infrastructure
Can reason through basic network troubleshooting
Separates application issues from connectivity issues
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Follow the traffic path from edge to app and check the control points in order: DNS, TLS, proxy, firewall, service routing, and application health.

nodes.name: Containers, Orchestration, and Deployment Platforms
core_concepts: EKS, GKE, AKS, ECS, and Docker Swarm
Autoscaling, rolling upgrades, and health checks

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how you would package and deploy a service in containers so that it is portable, horizontally scalable, and resilient during rolling updates and incidents.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why are readiness, liveness, and graceful shutdown more important than simply getting the container to boot successfully?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands container runtime and orchestration fundamentals
Can reason about pod lifecycle and deployment safety
Designs for resilience and service availability
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Think from the perspective of the traffic path and failure modes: what handles health, traffic routing, and restarts when a pod becomes unhealthy?

nodes.name: Cloud Platforms, IaC, and Provisioning
core_concepts: AWS, Azure, GCP, DigitalOcean, and hosting basics

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Describe how you would provision a scalable application stack in the cloud with repeatable infrastructure, environment separation, and a low-risk change process.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why is treating infrastructure as code a reliability requirement, not just a convenience feature, in modern systems?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands cloud provisioning and IaC principles
Knows how to separate environments and manage config
Treats infrastructure as safe, auditable, and repeatable
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Start with declarative definitions and reusable modules so the infrastructure can be reviewed, diffed, and recreated predictably.

nodes.name: Configuration Management and Secret Handling
core_concepts: Ansible, Chef, Puppet, and configuration drift management
Vault, Kubernetes Secrets, and external secret stores

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how you would rotate secrets and manage environment configuration for a production service without introducing downtime or leaving stale credentials in use.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do configuration and secret management failures often become system-wide reliability problems rather than isolated misconfigurations?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands secret lifecycle and secure configuration
Can reason about drift and environment correctness
Knows how to protect secrets and keep deployments predictable
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Use external secret stores, rotation workflows, and clear ownership boundaries so secrets are not embedded in code, scripts, or stale configs.

nodes.name: Monitoring, Observability, and Log Management
core_concepts: Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, New Relic, OpenTelemetry

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how you would instrument a production service with useful metrics, logs, and traces so you can detect latency and error spikes while correlating the issue back to the user-facing behavior.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do dashboards and alerts fail to prevent incidents when they only show symptoms and not the causal path or service dependencies?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands telemetry and observability fundamentals
Knows the difference between metrics, logs, and traces
Can connect monitoring signals to incident response and prevention
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Use the instrumentation to answer the questions: what is healthy, what is failing, and which dependency or pathway is responsible.

nodes.name: Artifact Management, Delivery, and GitOps
core_concepts: Nexus, Artifactory, Cloudsmith, and OCI concepts
GitOps patterns with ArgoCD and FluxCD
Release promotion and environment drift control

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Design a release workflow where application changes are versioned, promoted, and deployed through GitOps with auditability and rollback safety.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do release systems that rely on manual commands often drift over time, and how do GitOps models reduce that operational complexity?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands artifact lifecycle and deployment promotion
Can reason about declarative, auditable releases
Recognizes the value of predictable rollback and drift control
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Treat deployments as a versioned system state, not a manual step, so the desired state is always inspectable and reproducible.

nodes.name: Service Mesh, Traffic Control, and Resilience Patterns
core_concepts: Service mesh as a control plane for communication
Traffic routing, retries, timeouts, and circuit breaking
Policy enforcement at the mesh layer

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how a service mesh can improve resilience, traffic shaping, and security in a distributed system with many internal service-to-service calls.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do retries and circuit breakers often need to be coordinated at the infrastructure layer, not just inside each application?
key_evaluation_criteria: Knows when a service mesh adds real value
Understands resilience and policy enforcement in distributed systems
Can connect reliability patterns to incident prevention
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Do not add a mesh just for complexity; use it where traffic management, observability, or security policy crosses service boundaries in a meaningful way.

nodes.name: Incident Response, Reliability Engineering, and SRE Practice
core_concepts: SLOs, SLIs, SLAs, and error budgets
Incident management, action plans, and blameless culture
Operational excellence and human safety in systems

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Describe how you would handle a major incident in a production service, including detection, triage, coordination, mitigation, and a postmortem that improves the system rather than just assigning blame.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do the most effective incident responses combine technical debugging with clear communication and a blameless learning process?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands incident workflow and response rigor
Can define SLOs and error budgets in practice
Builds reliability through learning, not just quick fixes
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Treat an incident as a system behavior to be analyzed and improved; document the causal chain, mitigation, and follow-up actions clearly.

resources.title: DevOps and Platform Engineering Career Path

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: How would you increase platform reliability and developer productivity at scale without creating brittle self-service systems or compromising operational safety?
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why is platform maturity not just about new tools, but about making the right defaults and guardrails easy to adopt by everyone?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands platform engineering as a leverage point
Can balance autonomy with safety and standards
Creates sustainable operational excellence and growth
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Design for reliable defaults, internal platforms, and operational guardrails so teams can move faster without increasing systemic risk.
